convoLines.text: "We gave them a good burial. Doesn't feel like enough, does it?"
There — the story splits again. You mark the spot.
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"Wow." Ramadan looks hurt, then angry. "I share my food with you and this is what I get?"
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"It's quiet today. Wrong kind of quiet. That's the priority."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
It's quiet at the cache spot. Illari doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Hah. I — yeah. It helps, hearing that."
"We lost Scott, Omar and Elias this week. I keep setting out extra portions. Stupid."
They relax, a fraction. This is going well.
"I keep turning over the last thing Elias said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Nobody says Elias's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Still on what's been happening. No time to waste."
You show them Maypop — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I wish we had longer. Soon, yeah?"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about grief — we wandered off it, 4 days back. 'Hah. I — yeah. It helps, hearing that.'"
A long exhale. "I'll get there. Just needed a minute where I didn't have to be fine."
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Have you heard what they're calling Lockpick? Amy is pushing 'The Loud Bastard'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Alright, love. Go do what you need to do."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What's your first memory? Like, ever. The earliest thing. Not that it matters."
"Quick version — Three. That's young. The brain keeps what it needs, I guess."
"Funny thing: Mine's rural Vermont, I think — heat on pavement, someone's hand huge around mine. Or I invented it. First memories are half real and half the story you needed."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on your first memory."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
*Last time, they came at you for asking. That's not innocence talking. Hold your ground.*
"Nope. No." Sam shakes their head too fast. "I don't know where you're getting this."
You don't answer. The quiet turns pointed.
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Right. Well." That's the whole goodbye.
"Hah. Have you heard anything? About the taken. The pods. Anything at all."
They nod. "Okay."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"It's my sister, Jessica. Was taken at the Scattering. The boring half, they said — my sister, boring. I think about that every day. The pods get into my sleep some nights.
Row on row of them, humming like a held note -- and I wake up reaching for something that isn't there."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? It'll pass."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"Bring Us Something Interesting. They just... took Ramadan and Zoltan. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"I sharpen sticks down to nothing. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Maypop — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"About that question — What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed? ...yeah."
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
Whatever warmth was building cools to politeness.
"What are you getting at?" A glance away, then back. They're choosing their words now.
"Still on the worst thing you've done."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? I don't know, though."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
*They've deflected you before. The evidence needs to be heavier this time — one more thread before you speak.*
"I wasn't a veterinarian. I was a bartender. I wasn't protecting myself. I was protecting someone else."
The silence stretches a beat too long. They study their hands.
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"I tried the Maypop like you showed me. Didn't poison anyone, so that's a win. Mark my words."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that plant lesson."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Windfall. They just... took Zoltan and Ramadan. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"My part? I sharpen sticks down to nothing and stay ready."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Right. Go on, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You told me about that kitchen — morning light, three years old. Have any other memories come back since?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
A beat. Then, as if shaking something off:
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Sure — what's on your mind? Anyway, I should move."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "They took Zoltan and Ramadan — Windfall, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"I check the treeline every hour. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one!"
"Still nothing on Jessica. I told you about the pods -- I keep thinking about them. The humming. Some nights I'm sure it's a dream. Other nights I'm sure it's not."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? That's the truth of it."
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Bring Us Something Interesting. They just... took Zoltan and Nathan. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"As I said — Still on what's been happening."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Don't mind me. I'm having a whole argument in my head and losing."
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
*You know the counter-attack now — the anger IS the tell. It means the accusation landed. Don't flinch.*
Quiet for a long time. Then, barely audible: "I took 1× Stone. I won't do it again."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
*Last time, they came at you for asking. That's not innocence talking. Hold your ground.*
"Wait, wait —" Ramadan holds up a hand, smiling. "I can see exactly why that sounded wrong. No — it's like this..." The pieces slot into place. Of course.
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. I know the meadow edge, west of the creek — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"We were just talking. Nothing important."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"They took Zoltan and Nathan — Bring Us Something Interesting, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Maypop — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Actually, forget it."
